# Appeal of Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield — Appeals Department
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**From:** Skyler Foster
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-19**
- **Member:** Skyler Foster
- **Member ID:** W711189816
- **Reference number:** POC-BD05618334-73239
- **Service denied:** Hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914
- **Requesting surgeon:** Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery
- **Governing policy:** *Carelon Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Musculoskeletal — Joint Surgery* (https://guidelines.carelonmedicalbenefitsmanagement.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/PDF-Joint-Surgery-2025-11-15.pdf)

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for the hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914) requested by my surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist. The notice dated 2026-08-19 states that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. I am asking you to reconsider that decision.

I am writing because I believe the records already in my file address each of the criteria in the plan's own guideline. Below I have set out the plan's published language and, next to each item, the corresponding entry from my chart. Where the plan needs something further, I am glad to have my surgeon send it — but I would ask that you tell me specifically what is missing, since the denial notice does not identify any particular document.

## The plan's criteria and what my records show

**1. Symptoms.** The guideline states:

> "Moderate to severe hip pain (primarily in the groin) worsened by flexion activities (e.g., squatting or prolonged sitting) that interferes with activities of daily living and is not explained by another diagnosis"

My records document 18 months of progressive hip pain that is not relieved by rest. They describe sharp anterior groin pain with sitting and with pivoting, and that I cannot run or squat.

**2. Examination.** The guideline states:

> "Positive impingement sign on clinical examination, defined as pain elicited with 90 degrees of flexion and internal rotation and adduction of the femur OR with extension and external rotation"

My records document positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain. If the reviewer needs the specific maneuver and positions recorded at examination, Dr. Lindqvist can supply that detail from the office note: [date and description of provocative testing, per office note].

**3. Imaging showing cam impingement.** The guideline states:

> "Imaging studies (radiographs, MRI, or 3D computed tomography) show cam impingement evidenced by ONE or more of the following:"

That sentence introduces a list of findings that I have not been given a copy of, so I cannot address every item on it. One of the listed findings I do have is:

> "Femoral head-neck offset with an alpha angle greater than or equal to 55 degrees"

My MRI arthrogram of the hip dated 2026-07-21 reports cam-type femoroacetabular impingement with an **alpha angle of 68 degrees**. If the plan applied other conditions from that list in reaching its decision, I ask that you identify them in writing so they can be addressed directly.

**4. No advanced osteoarthritis.** The guideline states:

> "No evidence of advanced osteoarthritis, defined as Tönnis grade ≥ 2, or joint space < 2 mm"

The 2026-07-21 MRI arthrogram reports **joint space preserved, Tönnis grade 0**.

**5. No severe chondral damage.** The guideline states:

> "No evidence of severe (modified Outerbridge grade IV) chondral damage"

My imaging report contains no finding of severe chondral damage. The full report is available to the reviewer on request.

**6. Conservative management — content.** The guideline states:

> "Conservative management1 must include a combination of strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and correct underlying dysfunction, including physical therapy AND at least ONE complementary conservative treatment strategy."

My records document:
- **Supervised physical therapy** focused on core and hip stabilization with activity modification — 18 visits from 2026-03-31 to 2026-07-21, recorded in the physical therapy discharge note;
- **NSAIDs** for 6 months with inadequate relief;
- **Corticosteroid injection** on 2026-04-26, which gave 3 weeks of partial relief.

That is physical therapy plus more than one additional treatment.

**7. Conservative management — duration.** The guideline states:

> "Failure of conservative management for a duration of at least 12 weeks*, including avoidance of hip stretching or any activity that elicits or aggravates symptoms"

My supervised physical therapy ran **16 weeks**, from 2026-03-31 to 2026-07-21, with activity modification documented as part of the program. The guideline also provides:

> "*Less than the full duration of conservative management is permitted for an alpha angle greater than 65 degrees"

My alpha angle is 68 degrees, so even a shorter course would be permitted — but I completed 16 weeks.

**8. Full course completed.** The guideline states:

> "Patient has completed a full course of conservative management (as defined above) for the current episode of care"

The physical therapy course was completed and discharged on 2026-07-21, within the current episode of care.

**9. No significant improvement.** The guideline states:

> "Worsening of or no significant improvement in signs and/or symptoms upon clinical reevaluation"

My pain is documented as progressive over 18 months and unrelieved by rest. The NSAIDs gave inadequate relief and the injection gave only 3 weeks of partial relief. I still have sharp groin pain with sitting and pivoting and still cannot run or squat.

**10. Causal association between the impingement and the damage.** The guideline states:

> "Documentation of a likely causal association between the femoroacetabular impingement morphology and damage, e.g., a pistol-grip deformity with a tear of the acetabular labrum and articular cartilage damage in the anterosuperior quadrant"

My MRI arthrogram reports cam-type femoroacetabular impingement with an alpha angle of 68 degrees **together with an anterosuperior labral tear** — the cam morphology and the labral damage are documented in the same study, in the same region.

**11. Imaging report requirement.** The guideline states:

> "Imaging report. The provider shall submit a detailed imaging report for studies obtained within the past 12 months that correlates with clinical findings of the requested procedure."

My MRI arthrogram was performed on **2026-07-21**, less than one month before the denial date of 2026-08-19, and its findings match my symptoms and examination.

**12. Documentation of compliance with therapy.** The guideline states:

> "Documentation of compliance with a plan of therapy that includes elements from these areas is required where conservative management is appropriate."

My compliance is recorded in the physical therapy discharge note: 18 visits completed over a 16-week supervised course.

## What I am asking for

My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed, and the records in the file line up with the criteria the plan itself publishes. I respectfully ask you to:

1. Overturn the denial dated 2026-08-19 and authorize hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914; or
2. If any document is still considered missing, tell me and Dr. Lindqvist in writing exactly which item it is and which criterion it relates to, so it can be sent promptly; and
3. Identify the specific criteria the plan applied, including any items from the list introduced by the imaging criterion above that I have not been given.

I would also like a copy of the clinical review criteria used in this determination and the credentials of the reviewer who made it.

My denial notice states that my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of that notice, by **2027-02-15**, and I am submitting it before that date. I am sending this letter to the appeals address shown on my denial notice.

Thank you for taking another look at this. Please contact me at the phone number above if anything further would help.

Sincerely,

**Skyler Foster**
Member ID: W711189816
Reference number: POC-BD05618334-73239
[Signature]
[Date signed]

**Enclosures:** [Copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-19]; [MRI arthrogram report dated 2026-07-21]; [Physical therapy discharge note, 2026-03-31 to 2026-07-21]; [Office notes from Lindqvist, MD]; [Injection record dated 2026-04-26]
